summary: Cuma Ozkan works in religious studies, sinology, and Buddhist studies. He earned a Master of Arts at the University of Iowa under the supervision of Morten Schlütter (attested 2013).
Cunda studied under Ajahn Pasanno and Ajahn Amaro.

Cuong T. Mai specializes in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and sinology. He earned an MA at the University of Hawaiʻi and a PhD from Indiana University under John R. McRae (attested 2009), later serving as Adjunct Lecturer at the University of Vermont.

Cynthea J. Bogel works in Japanology, history and archaeology, and Buddhist studies. She studied under Keizaburo Mizuno and completed doctoral work under John M. Rosenfield, holding a post at the University of Washington (attested 2004–2009).

Cynthia Col specializes in sinology and religious studies. She was a student in Chinese religion at the Graduate Theological Union (attested 2003) and studied under Mark Elliott and Steven D. Goodman.
Cynthia M. Beall is a Tibetologist who studied at Pennsylvania State University circa 1971–1976. In 1976, she joined the faculty at Case Western Reserve University.
Cynthia Talbot is an Indologist and historian. She studied at the University of Wisconsin-Madison from circa 1977 to 1988 and took up a post at the University of Texas at Austin circa 1995.

Cyril Henry Philips was a historian and Indologist. He studied at the University of Liverpool (1931–1934) and SOAS (circa 1936–1940), later serving as SOAS Director from 1957 and Vice-Chancellor of the University of London (1972–1976).

Cyrus Stearns specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under Turrell V. Wylie, Dezhung Rinpoche, Chogye Trichen Rinpoche, Dilgo Khyentse, and earned a PhD under Leonard van der Kuijp at the University of Washington (1996), later working for Tsadra Foundation.

Cécile Ducher is a Tibetology and Buddhist studies scholar who completed her PhD at the École Pratique des Hautes Études under Matthew T. Kapstein by 2017. She has served as a research fellow at the École Pratique des Hautes Études.

D. C. Lau was a scholar of sinology and philosophy. He studied at the University of Hong Kong and University of Glasgow, later holding posts at SOAS, University College London, and The Chinese University of Hong Kong (1978–1989).
D. C. Sarasvati was an Indology scholar who studied under V. Raghavan (attested 1978). She served as a Lecturer-cum-Research Assistant at the University of Madras from 1964 to 1965.
D. Dennis Hudson was an Indologist and religious studies scholar. He spent his career at Smith College, teaching in the Department of Religion and Biblical Studies from circa 1970 to 2004.
D. L. Narasimhachar was an Indology and linguistics scholar. After studying at Maharaja's College, Mysore (circa 1925–1929), he held a post at the University of Mysore from circa 1932 to 1962.

D. Neil Schmid specializes in sinology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Waseda University, the École Pratique des Hautes Études, and the University of Pennsylvania, where he completed his doctoral studies under Victor H. Mair.
D. R. Nagaraj was an Indologist who studied at Bangalore University from circa 1972 to 1977. He subsequently held a post at Bangalore University from circa 1978 until 1998.

D. R. Shackleton Bailey was a classicist, Indologist, and Tibetologist educated at Cambridge. He held fellowships and lectureships at Cambridge (1944–1968), before serving on the faculties of the University of Michigan (1968–1976; 1988–2002) and Harvard University (1975–1988).
D. S. Subbaramaiya was an Indology and philosophy scholar who received traditional training under Mallikere Subrahmanya Sastri and V. S. Ramachandra Sastri.

D. Srinivasachar was an Indologist who served as Professor of Sanskrit at Maharaja's College, Mysore, and succeeded Rudrapatna Shamasastry as Curator at the Oriental Research Institute Mysore (attested 1931–1933).

Dagfinn Føllesdal was a philosopher and linguist. Educated at the University of Oslo and Harvard under Willard Van Orman Quine, he taught at Harvard (1961–1964) before long-term professorships at the University of Oslo (circa 1967–1999) and Stanford University (1968–2011).
